clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-month-old girl presented with petechiae on the soft palate, which progressed to a widespread hemorrhagic rash with a strong edematous component on the limbs, face, and auricles. This occurred following a mild febrile diarrheal episode and MMR vaccination. Initial workup ruled out ITP with a normal platelet count. During hospitalization, bilateral edema and pain in the metacarpophalangeal joints developed. Laboratory tests showed an elevated C-reactive protein (3.58 mg/dL) but no leukocytosis and continued normal platelet counts. While several other tests were collected (urinalysis, ESR, renal function, viral serologies, etc.), their specific results were not documented, nor were the findings of an ordered skin biopsy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: 15-month-old female presenting with petechiae on soft palate and a progressively increasing hemorrhagic rash.
The rash was characterized by petechial-hemorrhagic lesions with sharp merges of varying sizes localized to the limbs, face, and auricles, associated with a strong edematous component.
History of mild febrile diarrhea 8 days prior and MMR vaccine 12 days prior, suggesting a post-infectious or post-vaccination trigger.
Normal platelet counts (171,000/mmc3 initially, 180,000/mm3 during hospitalization) ruled out thrombocytopenia.
Elevated C-reactive protein (3.58 mg/dL) indicating systemic inflammation.
Bilateral edema of the metacarpophalangeal joints with joint pain appeared on the second day of hospitalization.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Normal platelet counts (171,000/mmc3 initially, 180,000/mm3 during hospitalization) explicitly ruled out this diagnosis.

While joint involvement was present, the specific rash morphology (large edematous plaques) is more typical for AHEI. Crucially, there is no documented evidence of renal involvement (hematuria/proteinuria) or significant abdominal symptoms, which are common in HSP.
